title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Price increase
drivers.evidence: Price up 3.4% vs regular; recent week at same price saw 1.05x baseline; no past promotion lift beyond noise; post-promo dip suggests demand pullback; conservative shrink toward 1.0.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 30.4. The target week has no events or promotions, but the price is raised to $5.20 (+3.4% vs $5.03). Recent weeks show no promotion, but sales rose to 32 units at $5.20 (2026-10-05), which is 1.05x baseline. Past promotions had weak noise-adjusted lift (x1.0) and post-promotion dips (x0.83). No evidence of price sensitivity beyond that. The classical model suggests no uplift, consistent with weak historical promotion effects. Price increase likely suppresses demand, but no direct evidence. Shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence and noise. The baseline already captures seasonal ramp (trend +16.2% over 13 weeks). No driver justifies a move from 1.0.

brief:
PRODUCT: Hot Cocoa Mix | category Grocery | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.20 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.03)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.4 | 5%-95%: 2.9 - 48.1 | 10%-90%: 7.6 - 47.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
